summary: Accepted the separate critic and independent coefficient/arithmetic checks. The declared one-switch family has exact pre-semiprime coefficient (2/d)*log((d-alpha)/alpha)<=-4/3, independent of beta; the explicitly refuted assertion is that this chosen family yields a positive lower coefficient. Preserved legal Wu-domain cutoffs, li(N) normalization, strict endpoints, m=1, repeated factors and global prime-divisor exceptions. Integrated the separately root-authored and reviewed nonnegative weighted parity model with exact g(p)=1/(p-1) at odd primes, summed all-log divisor errors through each fixed x^(1-epsilon), and zero odd-Omega population for the plus model. Its separately reviewed C=1 bilinear test at M=x^(2/5) is at least x/log(x)^2 before mass scaling, identifying additional correlation information absent from the model. None of these statements is a failure theorem for actual primes, all switching methods, or the full FI setup. No actual-prime parity lower margin, Goldbach proof, breakthrough or novelty claim is obtained. The active goal remains open; any next source bridge must supply genuinely additional parity-sensitive actual-prime input. The LWW prime-list manuscript is only a source under root inspection, with no theorem imported here.

claims.text: The assertion that this chosen one-switch family yields a positive leading lower coefficient for F_alpha is refuted by the exact coefficient M=(2/d)*log((d-alpha)/alpha)<=-4/3 in its declared domain.

The separately reviewed weighted parity model has exact shifted-prime divisor densities at odd primes with all-log summed error through every fixed level below 1, while its plus sequence has zero odd-factor population.

The separately reviewed concrete bilinear expression for that model at M=x^(2/5) has lower bound x/log(x)^2, and therefore distinguishes the model from any sequence satisfying a sufficiently small bound for that expression.
A positive parity-sensitive pointwise lower margin for actual prime complements, a Goldbach proof, an established breakthrough, and novelty remain unestablished.
